summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of chronic systolic heart failure, ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for shortness of breath and chest pain following a recent pacemaker implantation. He reported noncompliance with medications due to financial constraints. Evaluation revealed uncontrolled hypertension with a blood pressure of 153/112 mmHg, but no evidence of acute coronary syndrome. His symptoms improved with optimization of antihypertensive therapy, including restarting lisinopril at 20mg daily and adjusting hydralazine dosing to improve adherence. His heart failure was stable, with mild residual pulmonary edema on imaging and euvolemic status on exam. He was monitored for device function, which remained normal, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up to monitor renal function and medication management.
